strategy.title: Sell seven $1,500 five-page websites to local small businesses with missing or outdated sites, paid in full at order, built by a subcontracted freelance WordPress designer paid from settled client money
strategy.why: There are 36.2 million US small businesses (SBA Office of Advocacy 2026), so the buyer pool is not the constraint. $1,500 is at the bottom of published freelancer prices for a small-business site ($1,500-$7,000, WPZOOM updated 2026-09-28; $500-$5,000, dev.to 2026), and a freelancer can build it for about $500, leaving ~$956 per site after the subcontract and Stripe's 2.9% + 30c. Seven paid orders settle $10,500 and keep $6,543 after $3,500 subcontracting, $307 fees and $150 of sending tools, inside the $500 capital cap and ~10.5 owner hours (1.5 per sale) of the 17 allowed. Brain finds the prospects and writes and sends the outreach; the owner only takes the closing calls. What no source establishes is whether these buyers pay $1,500 from a cold email and how many do (demand, price, conversion), plus the designer's written quote; the first 300-contact wave measures those before the subcontract money is committed.

answers.resolution: Accepted: owner calls are now capped at 3.5 h per week (2 / 3.5 / 3.5 / 1 h across weeks 1-4), closes are spread to days 9-22, and scope is settled by email.

answers.finding: Calls with non-buyers are owner time; total owner hours are unknown, not 10.5.
answers.resolution: Accepted: calls with non-buyers count inside the weekly cap; total owner time is an ESTIMATE measured in week 1, and the stop rule now tests the weekly limit.

answers.resolution: Accepted: the freelancer quote is now an OWNER step (0.5 h, marketplace post), not a Brain step.

answers.finding: Price $1,500 rests on generic freelancer ranges (WPZOOM $1,500-$7,000; dev.to $500-$5,000); correctly left to the test. q_tools $150 is an unpriced estimate.
answers.resolution: Accepted: price and the $150 tools stay ESTIMATE; tools spend is capped at $150 and is the only pre-proof money.

strategy.title: Sell seven $1,500 five-page websites to local small businesses with missing or outdated sites, paid in full at order, built by a subcontracted freelance WordPress designer paid from settled client money
strategy.why: There are 36.2 million US small businesses (SBA Office of Advocacy 2026), so the buyer pool is not the constraint. $1,500 is at the bottom of published freelancer prices for a small-business site ($1,500-$7,000, WPZOOM updated 2026-09-28; $500-$5,000, dev.to 2026), and a freelancer can build it for about $500, leaving ~$956 per site after the subcontract and Stripe's 2.9% + 30c. Seven paid orders settle $10,500 and keep $6,543 after $3,500 subcontracting, $307 fees and $150 of sending tools, inside the $500 capital cap and at most 3.5 owner hours in any week (10.5 in all, under the 4 h/week limit). Brain finds the prospects and writes and sends the outreach; the owner requests the designer quote and takes short closing calls, capped per week. What no source establishes is whether these buyers pay $1,500 from a cold email and how many do (demand, price, conversion), plus the designer's written quote; the first 300-contact wave measures those before the subcontract money is committed.
